events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.93)
events.body:
The cancellation was made by the rider [F2], so the fee can only stand through NS-0's rider branch, which routes an on-demand booking to NS-4 [NS-0]. NS-4 makes a rider cancellation free only if it happens within 3 minutes of matching, and chargeable only after that; here acceptance was 18:23:00 and cancellation 18:25:30, i.e. 2 min 30 s (150 s) after matching [F2], so no cancellation fee was payable and the $6.61 on the fare record [F5] must be refunded in full [NS-4][NS-7].

The no-show branch does not rescue the fee either. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival [F4], and driver_arrived_at is null [F3], so NS-1(i) is not satisfied; the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 1816 m and he never came within 200 m [F1], so the GPS-at-pickup condition NS-1(ii) fails; and with no arrival there was no continuous 3-minute wait after a tap, so NS-1(iii) fails too [NS-1]. Any one failure of NS-1 sends the fee to a full refund under NS-2 [NS-2]. The driver's chat at 18:24 saying "5 min more, traffic is slow" [F8] and his post-trip statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F10] are consistent with him being nowhere near; in any event a statement cannot outweigh a GPS record, which places him 1816 m away at the moment of cancellation [F1][F3][F4].

The congestion material does not create an exemption: there were no recorded traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F12], and the only speed record is band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Jurong East Avenue 1, which is neither an incident nor a severe-congestion band corroborating one [F11] (weather was fair, 0.0 mm [F13]). In any case NS-4 governs a rider cancellation inside the 3-minute window regardless of driver lateness, and Ryde publishes no driver-late-vs-ETA waiver rule [NS-4][NS-7].

The amount is fixed by the fare record: the cancellation fee charged is $6.61 with no surge (1.0×), so the refund is $6.61 [F5][F6][NS-2]. No account flag arises: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" at a location outside the pickup radius, because he never pressed it at all [F4], and the profiles on both sides show 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F14][F15], so NS-2's flag condition and RD-6 are not triggered [NS-2][NS-7].

Safety screen: I read every message in the record — rider "How long will you be?" [F7], driver "5 min more, traffic is slow" [F8], and the driver's written statement [F10] — and the complaint as filed. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the exchange is a routine pickup-timing query. No RD-3/RD-5 segment findings arise because this is not a route-deviation case.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: Good news — your $6.61 cancellation fee is being refunded in full as a Ryde voucher.

Why: you cancelled just two and a half minutes after you were matched, and the first three minutes are free. The driver also never marked himself as arrived at the pickup point, and his location showed he was still well away from you, so no waiting fee could apply either.

Nothing further is needed from you. The voucher will be credited to your account. Your record stays clean — no flags or penalties.

DRIVER: Your $6.61 cancellation fee is not payable, so we are refunding it to the rider as a Ryde voucher and it will not be credited to you.

Why: the rider cancelled two and a half minutes after being matched, which falls inside the free-cancellation window. You also never marked yourself as arrived at the pickup point, and our location records placed you about 1.8 km away — so no waiting fee could be charged.

No action is required from you and no flag has been added to your account.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7) within the dispute window.
ruling.reasoning:
The cancellation was made by the rider [F2], so the fee can only stand through NS-0's rider branch, which routes an on-demand booking to NS-4 [NS-0]. NS-4 makes a rider cancellation free only if it happens within 3 minutes of matching, and chargeable only after that; here acceptance was 18:23:00 and cancellation 18:25:30, i.e. 2 min 30 s (150 s) after matching [F2], so no cancellation fee was payable and the $6.61 on the fare record [F5] must be refunded in full [NS-4][NS-7].

The no-show branch does not rescue the fee either. The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival [F4], and driver_arrived_at is null [F3], so NS-1(i) is not satisfied; the driver's closest approach to the pickup was 1816 m and he never came within 200 m [F1], so the GPS-at-pickup condition NS-1(ii) fails; and with no arrival there was no continuous 3-minute wait after a tap, so NS-1(iii) fails too [NS-1]. Any one failure of NS-1 sends the fee to a full refund under NS-2 [NS-2]. The driver's chat at 18:24 saying "5 min more, traffic is slow" [F8] and his post-trip statement "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" [F10] are consistent with him being nowhere near; in any event a statement cannot outweigh a GPS record, which places him 1816 m away at the moment of cancellation [F1][F3][F4].

The congestion material does not create an exemption: there were no recorded traffic incidents near the route during the trip window [F12], and the only speed record is band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Jurong East Avenue 1, which is neither an incident nor a severe-congestion band corroborating one [F11] (weather was fair, 0.0 mm [F13]). In any case NS-4 governs a rider cancellation inside the 3-minute window regardless of driver lateness, and Ryde publishes no driver-late-vs-ETA waiver rule [NS-4][NS-7].

The amount is fixed by the fare record: the cancellation fee charged is $6.61 with no surge (1.0×), so the refund is $6.61 [F5][F6][NS-2]. No account flag arises: the driver never pressed "I'm Here" at a location outside the pickup radius, because he never pressed it at all [F4], and the profiles on both sides show 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days [F14][F15], so NS-2's flag condition and RD-6 are not triggered [NS-2][NS-7].

Safety screen: I read every message in the record — rider "How long will you be?" [F7], driver "5 min more, traffic is slow" [F8], and the driver's written statement [F10] — and the complaint as filed. There is no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation; the exchange is a routine pickup-timing query. No RD-3/RD-5 segment findings arise because this is not a route-deviation case.

rejected_claims.reason: Not rejected as an outcome, but its legal route is wrong: the driver's non-arrival [F3][F4] goes to the NS-1 no-show branch, which fails; the charge itself is governed by NS-4 because the cancellation was rider-initiated within 3 minutes [F2] — NS-1 is not the clause that decides the fee here.

The GPS point is accurate but it is applied to the wrong test: the 200 m radius under NS-1(ii) is only an element of a driver-claimed no-show cancellation, which the driver never made; the decisive provision is NS-4 [F1][F2].

Correct on the facts (no incidents [F12], band 4 only [F11]) but immaterial to liability: the rider-cancellation rule in NS-4 does not turn on congestion or on RD-4-style exemptions, so the traffic findings cannot carry or defeat the refund claim [NS-4].

The outcome is right but the cited clause is not: NS-3 concerns a driver cancelling without a valid reason, which did not happen here — the cancellation was by the rider [F2], so NS-0 routes the case to NS-4, not NS-3.

Its non-flag request is accepted, but the records it relies on (profile history [F15], complete timestamped chat [F9]) are confirmatory only; the ground for refusing a flag against the driver is that he never pressed the arrival button at all [F4], so NS-2's wrong-location flag condition is unmet [NS-2].

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after matching (accepted 18:23:00, cancelled by rider 18:25:30), i.e. within the 3-minute grace period, so no cancellation fee is payable.
The driver never arrived: the platform recorded no arrival at the pickup point and the driver never pressed "I'm Here", so the no-show precondition for any fee is absent.
GPS shows the driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 1816 m at 18:25:30 and he never came within 200 m, confirming the rider was right that the driver was nowhere near.

The driver's own chat message at 18:24 said "5 min more", consistent with him still being minutes away, and his later written statement only says he "was on my way" — neither establishes arrival or continuous waiting at the pickup point.
No congestion excuse can rescue the fee: traffic records show no incidents near the route and only band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Jurong East Avenue 1, with fair weather and no rain.
The $6.61 already charged on the fare record should be refunded in full as an unsupported cancellation fee.

weaknesses: The driver may argue the rider was not entitled to free cancellation merely because he had not yet arrived, since Ryde publishes no 'driver late vs ETA' waiver rule (NS-8 is informational only); our answer is the 3-minute rule in NS-4.

Traffic on Jurong East Avenue 1 was band 4 (30–39 km/h) and the driver said 'traffic is slow' (F8, F11): the judge may view the delay as excusable, though band 4 is not severe congestion and F11 is not incident evidence under RD-4-style corroboration, and neither affects the 3-minute rule.

There is no GPS sampling history between 18:23 and 18:25 besides the closest-approach summary (F1), so the exact movement of the driver during the grace period is not detailed; the summary is still a system record and it contradicts arrival.
Profile facts are clean on both sides (F14, F15) and give no support for a flag_account request against the driver in this case.

claims.assertion: The rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after matching, which is within the 3-minute grace window, so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable and the rider is entitled to a full refund of that fee (F2, F5).

The driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, so the no-show branch that could justify the fee (driver waits >3 min at the pickup point after arrival confirmation) was never triggered (F4, F3).

The driver's closest approach to the pickup point was 1816 m and he never came within 200 m, so at no point during the 2 min 30 s could the driver have satisfied the GPS-at-pickup condition for a no-show cancellation fee (F1, F4).

The driver's own contemporaneous message says he was still "5 min more" away at 18:24, which corroborates that he was still en route and not present at the pickup point when the rider cancelled at 18:25:30 (F8, F2).

No exemption rescues the fee: there are no recorded traffic incidents on the route, only a moderate speed band (30–39 km/h) on Jurong East Avenue 1 and fair weather, so the delay is congestion, not an event justifying a no-show cancellation fee (F11, F12, F13).

Because the rider cancelled inside the 3-minute window, NS-3's rule that the rider bears no cancellation fee once the no-show conditions fail applies, so the fee on record must be refunded rather than left standing (F2, F5).

The refund should be issued as a $6.61 Ryde voucher and no account flag is sought against my client: the driver never pressed the Here button at a place other than the pickup point (F4), has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days over 1043 trips (F15), and the chat record is complete with every message timestamped (F9).

weaknesses: The driver's post-trip statement claims "I was on my way when the rider cancelled" (F10), but the GPS record puts his closest approach at 1816 m (F1) — the statement alone cannot carry weight against the system record, so I do not rely on it.

The driver's own message told the rider "5 min more, traffic is slow" (F8) while the cancellation fee of $6.61 stood on record (F5); the rider will argue, and NS-4 supports, that a rider who is told to expect a 5-minute wait will treat a fee charged at 2:30 as unfair, so my client gains nothing on this point.

Nothing in the traffic facts shows a qualifying incident (only a 30–39 km/h speed band, F11/F12), so no "reasonable cause" argument can be built to justify the driver's position on the fee or his lateness.
Profile facts (F15, F14) can only support an outcome or an account flag, never decide the case, so a favourable driver history cannot supply the main finding.

points.response: Conceded — the rider cancelled 2 min 30 s after acceptance (F2), inside the 3-minute grace period, so the $6.61 on the fare record (F5) is not chargeable under NS-4. The driver's brief agrees with the rider's C1 on the decisive point.
No dispute: no arrival confirmation was ever recorded and the driver never tapped "I'm Here" (F3, F4), so the NS-1 no-show branch never opened and NS-2 requires the fee be refunded in full (F5).

Agreed and noted in the rider's favour: the driver's closest approach was 1816 m and he never entered the 200 m radius (F1), so the GPS-at-pickup condition of NS-1 fails on the only system record of driver position.

This corroborates the rider's C4: the driver said "5 min more" at 18:24 (F8) yet the fee stood on a 2 min 30 s cancellation (F2), so under the system-record-wins rule his later "on my way" statement (F10) cannot manufacture an arrival.

Accepted as far as it goes: no incidents, only band 4 (30–39 km/h) and fair weather (F11, F12, F13), so nothing exempts the fee and NS-2 governs; the driver's own explanation of slow traffic is therefore irrelevant to liability.

Conceded in substance, but the correct route is NS-0/NS-2 with NS-4 as an alternative: because the 3-minute grace period applied (F2) and the no-show conditions failed (F3, F4, F1), the $6.61 already charged (F5) must be refunded in full.

The rider does not contest the voucher form under NS-7, and no flag_account is pressed: the driver never pressed "Here" at the wrong place (F4) and has 0 upheld disputes in 90 days over 1043 trips (F15), so a $6.61 voucher refund is the whole remedy.

Conceded: the cancellation at 18:25:30 is 2 min 30 s after the 18:23:00 acceptance (F2), inside the 3-minute window, so under NS-4 the fee is not chargeable and my client's position on the outcome is the same as the rider's.

Agreed and independently established by the driver's side: no arrival confirmation exists on record (F4) and driver_arrived_at is null (F3), so NS-1's precondition for a no-show fee was never met — a finding that follows from the system records, not from anyone's statement.
Agreed: the closest approach of 1816 m at 18:25:30 (F1) is a GPS record and it confirms the driver was not at the pickup point, which removes the NS-1 (ii) GPS condition entirely.

Conceded: the 18:24 message "5 min more, traffic is slow" (F8) and the post-trip statement (F10) show only that the driver was still en route and do not establish arrival or waiting; the rider is right that no statement-based case exists for my client.

Conceded: the traffic facts show only band 4 (30–39 km/h) on Jurong East Avenue 1 with no incidents and fair weather (F11, F12, F13), so no exemption under NS-1 can be built on congestion and my client does not rely on the driver's "traffic is slow" message (F8).

Agreed as to the amount: $6.61 charged on the fare record (F5) with a 1.0× surge multiplier (F6) must be refunded in full under NS-2, issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7; no flag_account action is appropriate against either party, since the driver never pressed "I'm Here" at a wrong location (F4) and both profiles show 0 disputes and 0 upheld over 90 days (F14, F15).
